packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-08 - unverified blind image reading (reader D)

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE NOTES
- No proposed identification or earlier reading of this fragment was in my
  context.
- Beyond the brief: in my scratchpad folder (readerD/) I rotated image-002 by
  180 deg (the text is upside down as photographed), boosted contrast and
  enlarged it 2-3x; I also contrast-boosted image-004. No other files.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
- image-001 (overview, labelled "B") and image-003 (overview of the other
  face): a small boat-shaped parchment offcut, c. 11 x 2.5 cm, with a twisted
  tongue at one end and a small tab on the long edge. Probably a binding
  strip cut from a leaf (tentative).
- Face in image-001/002: text written UPSIDE DOWN relative to the photo.
  Six partial lines of small, rather cursive gothic script in faded brown
  ink. Short red vertical strokes occur at intervals in the lines (red
  touching of capitals or red paraph/stroke marks). Line beginnings and
  ends are lost (the piece is cut on all sides); only one column visible.
  A pale blue-white smear crosses the centre (later stain or adhesive).
- Face in image-003/004: dark, abraded, with small red strokes (red touches)
  visible but no legible text even after enhancement.
- No rubrics, initials, glosses or headings visible.

TRANSCRIPTION (image-002.jpg, read after 180 deg rotation; lines counted
from the top of the rotated image; each line truncated at both ends)
  l.1   [..]ori? ou(?)ie? / an(im)e? ip(s)a? [..]
  l.2   [..]bore? studium? / sudaru(m)? . uita? / ui(r)tus? . [..] hoc? tuo? [..]
  l.3   p(ro)? eo (et)? (?)rabon(?) / labore? [..] ma(teri)a? ei? mali? [..] cienes? / b(e)ne sciens? [..]
  l.4   [..]tatue? / [..]tatur . Vir? / Qui? (et) ther? [..]ui? [..] q(uod)? i(n)? [..]p(?)ormie? / formice? . A(?)x? [..]
  l.5   [..] amore (?) (et)? an(im)i? [..] uirtute? [..] (?)capi(?)s? [..] sacramento? / sa(?)c(?)ndo? [..]
  l.6   amore? n(on)? . nolebit? / uolebit? [..]e(?)ne(?) [..] aq(?)ui? mali uoluntate? / malitia? [..]
  (red strokes fall at: l.2 centre, l.3 centre-left, l.4 right, l.5-6 lower
   left and right; I cannot tell whether they mark capitals or punctuation)

image-004.jpg (other face): [illegible] throughout; only red strokes and
  abrasion visible.

SELECTED / UNREAD
- All six lines of the readable face were attempted; essentially nothing is
  secure. The words "amore" (l.5 and l.6) and "mali" (l.3, l.6) are the most
  confident; everything else is a letter-shape guess. It is not even certain
  the language is Latin.
- Unread: the entire other face.

LIMITATIONS
- Very faded ink, small script, tiny fragment cut on all sides.
- Suggest UV / multispectral imaging of both faces; the other face may
  retain text invisible under normal light.
